content.text:
Cursor does have a Projects feature, but you have to create the Project in the app. The docs describe no CLI, API, or SDK call for creating a Project or linking a repo to one. On top of that, `/Users/tharrop/Documents/Semiconductor` isn't a git repo (there's no `.git`), so it can't be picked as a Project's workspace until it has a remote.

**1. What Projects is and where it lives.** From [Projects](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/projects): "A Project takes on a larger body of work, such as a feature, a migration, or a full app. You direct it by chatting with its coordinator agent… Projects live in the left-hand nav of the Agents Window and run on Cloud Agents." The coordinator plans the work and hands it to worker agents. The Project also keeps a shared context store that every agent in it can read and write.
- **Plans:** It needs a plan that includes Cloud Agents: Premium or higher, Teams, Enterprise, or a legacy paid plan. It isn't available on Free, Plus, or legacy Hobby, or with Privacy Mode (Legacy). Enterprise teams need Cursor 3.21.9 or later.
- **Where:** Projects aren't in the classic editor or the cursor.com dashboard. Open the Agents Window with Cmd+Shift+P → **Open Agents Window** ([Agents Window](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agents-window)).

**2. Creating and naming a Project** (UI steps from the docs):
1. In the Agents Window sidebar, find the **Projects** section and click **New Project**.
2. Choose an icon and enter the name, for example "Semiconductor and Electronics". If you leave it empty, it's called "New Project".
3. Under **Workspace**, pick the repository. Under **Model**, pick the coordinator's model.
4. Click **Create Project**. It opens as a chat with the coordinator.

**3. Associating a repository.** You pick the repo when you create the Project. The docs say "Projects run in the cloud, so the list shows the repositories available to your cloud agents. If GitHub isn't connected yet, the menu offers Connect GitHub." So in practice the repo needs a remote that cloud agents can reach. A local-only folder won't show up. Cloud agents support GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps, and they also work with Cursor-hosted Origin repos ([Origin agents](https://cursor.com/docs/origin/agents)). The Projects page itself only mentions GitHub, so I can't confirm from the docs that Origin repos appear in the Workspace picker.

You can also bring existing chats into a Project. Drag an eligible Cloud Agent chat onto the Project row, or use the chat's menu → **Add to Project**. Cursor converts a local chat to Remote Control first.

**4. Programmatic options.** None for the Project itself. The [Cloud Agents API](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints) covers agents, environments, secrets, and automations, but has no Projects endpoints. One small hint: the Automations endpoints say "Project routines aren't listed". The only part an agent can do is the step before:
- **Origin repo:** Per [Create an Origin repository](https://cursor.com/docs/origin/create-repository), an agent can install the Origin CLI, sign in, run `origin repo create`, set the remote, and push. Alternatively, create it in the UI at [cursor.com/codebase](https://cursor.com/codebase) → **New**.
- **GitHub repo:** Push the folder to GitHub, then connect GitHub in Cursor.

So the order is: run `git init`, add a remote and push, then the user runs the four UI steps above and picks the repo under **Workspace**.

I'm noticing Origin repo support isn't spelled out in the Projects docs, which only mention "repositories available to your cloud agents" and a "Connect GitHub" option. There's also a Cloud Agents API error code, `origin_not_enabled`, that hints Origin cloud-agent use might be switched off per team.
